Initialize the story display, CIA timer, encoded-text keys, interrupt vectors and intro music. The outer depacker and drive-code upload have already finished.
Install eight sprite shapes $10-$17 and clear the generated $0400-$05FF text image.
Unpack page zero before enabling raster interrupts; set the third rolling text key to $D3.
Select one of sixteen pictures. Later pages optionally clear the workspace, then unpack, draw and fade in.
Read both joystick ports and leave on fire; otherwise wait for the IRQ text reader to signal its next $FF marker.
Apply the selected fade-out flag and advance the picture index; sixteen pictures finish the story.

Leaving on fire: call the attribute routine with A zero, which copies the staged attributes over the screen again and leaves the picture showing, then step the eight text sprites through the twenty colours at $A287, last entry first, one a frame at raster line $64, before the loading display.
With I/O hidden, copy the loading IRQ to $CC00, eight sprite bitmaps to $D800 and the host loader from $A818 to $6900-$6BFF.
Use sprite shapes $60-$67, copy the loading sprite positions, change the IRQ to $CC00 and jump through the $CC78 entry vector.
Little-endian $7D7E, the vector used by JMP ($7CA7) at $A244. $7D7E holds a jump to the story-byte reader at $7FD0.
Discard the nested IRQ return address bytes, switch the video bank and perform the timed lower-border display sequence.
Twenty raster-timed horizontal-scroll register pairs with fixed instruction delays.
Update intro music once, restore the picture display and advance the text sprites; joystick-left doubles the scroll call.
Schedule the first raster handler again and restore bank port and interrupted A/X/Y.
Save registers and processor-port state, set up the nested raster interrupt and wait in the timing region.

Jump to the story-byte reader at $7FD0. This is the address held in the vector at $7CA7, so every character read (jsr $A244, jmp ($7CA7)) passes through here. It also follows the twenty NOPs of the first raster handler, which the nested interrupt normally cuts short.
Insert a new decoded character every eight calls. $FF advances the picture flag and is consumed immediately; zero would leave the source pointer unchanged.

Codes $61 and above have $20 subtracted, selecting the lowercase glyphs $41-$5A; other characters use their low six bits, so capitals select glyphs $01-$1A. Multiply by eight and add the font base $91AC.
Insert eight source rows into the last sprite with three-byte row spacing.
Rotate eight three-byte sprite columns through carry across eight pixel rows, moving the text through $0400-$05FF.
Incremented for an encrypted $FF story marker, consumed by the foreground picture loop.
Reloaded with seven between inserted character columns; the sprite pixels rotate on every scroll call.
High-byte accumulator while multiplying a decoded glyph index by eight.
Copy the unpacked $C000 picture rows to the directory-selected bitmap position. Rows advance by 320 bytes.
Fill matching rows in the $BB00 attribute staging area using each page colour pair.
Pages seven and eight omit the frame; all others draw the eight border pieces and frame colour attributes.
Draw top-left corner, repeated top edge and top-right corner.
Walk the picture height, adding left/right bitmap sides and their attributes.
Draw the bottom attribute row and bottom-left, repeated bottom edge and bottom-right bitmap pieces.
Decode ((source XOR $0277) minus $0801) XOR $1B with explicit SEC. Update $1B by XOR, add it to $0801, then XOR the result into $0277. Live read-watch and instruction steps gave first character $20.
Nine zero bytes between text decoder and music entry points.
Jump to the separate intro music song initializer.
Jump to the per-frame intro song driver.
Jump to $8257, which installs the driver's own raster interrupt at $0314/$0315 and sets the stopped state $C0. The intro never calls this entry.
ASCII ROMUZAK89 signature of the separate intro music driver.
Three little-endian bases for the song headers, pattern pointers and eight-byte instrument records.

Two filter constants the driver only reads: $8018 is the cutoff a note with instrument flag $20 starts from (copied to $808E), and $8019 is the step subtracted from the cutoff on each update of such a voice.

The step, $1A, subtracted from the filter cutoff at $808E on each update of a voice whose instrument has flag $20 (sbc $8019 at $8728). The driver only reads it. With $8018, the cutoff such a note starts from, it is one of two filter constants.
Three order-stream byte indices.
Three pattern-stream byte indices.

Three current instrument numbers, one a voice. Loaded from the pattern-selected instrument at $809F,x when a note starts, or from an instrument chain; multiplied by eight to index the records at $8AF6.
Three rest flags, one a voice: a rest command ($80-$9F) stores 8, a new note clears it, and while it is nonzero the voice skips its instrument effects.
Three portamento selectors.
Three repeat counters.
Three signed note transpositions.
Three order-selected instrument offsets.

Per-voice state of the intro music driver, in groups of three bytes indexed by the voice number (X = 0 to 2): durations, notes, order and pattern positions, pulse, filter and modulation values. The per-voice groups are $8032-$8043, $8045-$806E, $8075-$8086, $8088-$808D, $8092-$809D and $809F-$80A1. The single bytes between them are shared by the three voices. $806F is a divide-by-two counter: the frame call decrements it at $82F9 and, each time it passes zero, reloads it with one and counts the three duration bytes $803E-$8040 down, so durations run at half the frame rate. $8070 is the play state: bit 6 marks a start or stop request the next frame call acts on ($82B7-$82E0), and bit 7 means stopped. $808E is the filter cutoff high byte, written to $D416 at $8A30. No instruction names $8044, which holds $FF. $8071-$8074, $8087, $808F-$8091 and $809E have notes of their own.

Ten-bit frame counter in two bytes: $82E3 increments $8071 on every frame call and carries into $8072, which is kept to its low two bits. Song selection at $82AA sets both bytes to one. Their OR is stored in $8073.

OR of the two frame-counter bytes $8071 and $8072, stored at $82F6: zero on one frame call in 1024. On that frame $89D5 lets the value at $808F be added to each voice's transposition and instrument offset. Song selection sets it to one.
Set to one, with $8071-$8073, when a song is selected ($82B3). No instruction in the intro reads it.

Index of the voice being processed. The frame call sets it to two at $830E, $8311 loads it into X for each voice, and $8A20 counts it down after the voice is written; when it goes negative the driver writes the volume and filter registers and returns.

Value added to each voice's transposition and instrument offset on the one frame call in 1024 when $8073 is zero ($89DE, $89E8). It stays zero while the credit text at $8208 checks out; a pass of the check at $89EE that does not end in $56 stores its result EOR $E2 here, which detunes the song.

Index of the credit-text check at $89EE: its low seven bits select the byte of $8208-$8287 read on this voice update. $8A17 increments it and $8A0C sets it back to zero when a pass ends at the $EA byte.
Running XOR of the credit-text bytes read by the check at $89EE. At the end of a pass $89FE compares it with $56, and $8A09 clears it for the next pass.

Shift counter used while a note's vibrato step is worked out, shared by the three voices: $8820 loads it with the low three bits of instrument byte five and $884D counts it down, halving the frequency difference of two neighbouring notes once for each count.
Ninety-five little-endian note-frequency entries before the waveform sequence directory.
Eight little-endian pointers to waveform/pitch byte sequences.

Waveform/pitch sequence at $8170, the stream of pointer 4 in the $8160 table (an instrument selects it with byte four = 4). Pairs of SID control byte and offset added to the frequency high byte; $FF ends the stream, which then holds, or restarts when instrument flag $40 is set.

Waveform/pitch sequence at $817D, the stream of pointer 0 in the $8160 table (an instrument selects it with byte four = 0). Pairs of SID control byte and offset added to the frequency high byte; $FF ends the stream, which then holds, or restarts when instrument flag $40 is set.

Byte eleven of the waveform/pitch sequence at $817D, the stream of pointer 0 in the $8160 table. The address is named only as the base of the credit-text check at $89F6, lda $8188,X with X from $80 to $FF, which reads $8208-$8287 and never this sequence.

Waveform/pitch sequence at $8194, the stream of pointer 1 in the $8160 table (an instrument selects it with byte four = 1). Pairs of SID control byte and offset added to the frequency high byte; $FF ends the stream, which then holds, or restarts when instrument flag $40 is set.

Waveform/pitch sequence at $81A5, the stream of pointer 2 in the $8160 table (an instrument selects it with byte four = 2). Pairs of SID control byte and offset added to the frequency high byte; $FF ends the stream, which then holds, or restarts when instrument flag $40 is set.

Waveform/pitch sequence at $81B0, the stream of pointer 3 in the $8160 table (an instrument selects it with byte four = 3). Pairs of SID control byte and offset added to the frequency high byte; $FF ends the stream, which then holds, or restarts when instrument flag $40 is set.
Waveform/pitch command sequence 5. The reader follows this stream through the selected $8160 pointer; $FF terminates the sequence.
Waveform/pitch command sequence 6. The reader follows this stream through the selected $8160 pointer; $FF terminates the sequence.
Waveform/pitch command sequence 7. The reader follows this stream through the selected $8160 pointer; $FF terminates the sequence.
SID voice-register offsets zero, seven and fourteen.
Voice-dependent filter masks $F1/$F2/$F4.

Three fixed frequency-high bases, one a voice, copied from instrument byte six when a note starts. With instrument flag $08 a wave sequence adds its offsets to this value instead of the note's frequency high byte.
Three signed note-state flags.

ASCII driver credit: "** ROMUZAK V6.3 <W> BY OLIVER BLASNIK, <C> DIGITAL MARKETING!! 02435-1295!! **", followed by a NOP byte ($EA). The driver checks this text: $89EE XORs the bytes from $8209 one a voice update, the $EA ends a pass, and the result must be $56.

Install the driver's own raster interrupt: point $0314/$0315 at the wrapper $8279, stop CIA1 timer A, enable the raster interrupt at line 1, then set the state $C0, at which the next frame call clears the three voice controls and the driver stays silent. The intro never calls this. This driver is separate from the flight/title/ending music engine.

Operand byte 2 of the JMP instruction at $8276, in the intro's code. Instructions in this part that name it: lda at $825E (read). The read copies the byte, $82, to the IRQ vector's high byte at $0315, after $79 goes to $0314: the vector is the wrapper at $8279.
Wrapper around the frame player; the surrounding entry bytes also provide constants to the stop setup.
Multiply A by six, copy the three order pointers from $8A46 and request state $40 restart. The story calls this with zero.
Inspect restart/stop flags, clear SID voice controls on restart and initialize the three voice states before processing tempo.
Process voices from X=2 down to zero using SID offsets fourteen, seven and zero. Duration expiry advances patterns/orders.
Read the current order byte. $80-$BF set signed transpose; $C0-$FB set a signed instrument offset; $FC jumps to a byte index, $FF restarts the order, and $FE/$FD change the stop/restart state.
Operand byte 1 of the SBC instruction at $8361, in the intro's code. Instructions in this part that name it: sta at $835B (write).
Operand byte 1 of the SBC instruction at $83A5, in the intro's code. Instructions in this part that name it: sta at $839F (write).

Convert the order pattern number to its little-endian source pointer. $FF ends the pattern and updates repeat/order indices; lower note bytes and the upper command groups set duration, instrument, gate, portamento or vibrato.
Select an eight-byte instrument, reset note-age, waveform, pulse, filter and modulation caches and prepare its SID registers.

Store instrument byte six (patched into the operand at $8552) as the voice's fixed frequency-high base at $8202, look up the note frequency at $80A2 and cache it. Portamento can preserve the previous live frequency. High instrument flags select the initial noise/wave and filter behaviour.
Operand byte 1 of the LDA instruction at $8551, in the intro's code. Instructions in this part that name it: sta at $84F9 (write).
Advance instrument-age effects, dispatching waveform sequence, arpeggio, pulse, filter, pitch and instrument-chain behaviour from the selected flags.
Read the selected waveform/pitch byte sequence through the $8160 pointer table.
Operand byte 1 of the LDA instruction at $85F8, in the intro's code. Instructions in this part that name it: sta at $85DC (write).
Select an instrument-relative arpeggio byte using the cyclic sequence position.
Alternate the note interval for the behaviour whose low mode bits equal four.
At the configured age threshold, chain the instrument selector when mode bits equal twelve.
Apply the constant pulse step for bit $10 and filter step for bit $20 in the instrument flags.

For instruments with both high flag bits set, alternate on each update between noise (control $81 at the frequency high byte in instrument byte six) and the instrument's own control byte at the note frequency, then write the SID directly; the slide, vibrato and pulse sweep are passed over.
Update note frequency and portamento according to the cached mode and signed step.
Select frequency sweep for mode eight; otherwise update the vibrato accumulators and sign at the instrument-defined rate.
Use the instrument pulse byte low count and high step to evolve the pulse width.
Use the instrument pitch byte count and scaled step for the frequency sweep.
Write the selected voice control, pulse and frequency registers, then update cached order transposition at its scheduled tick.

Check the credit text at $8208. On each voice update read one byte through base $8188 with index ($8090 AND $7F) EOR $80, which reaches $8208-$8287, and XOR it into $8091. The $EA byte at $8256, the first with bit 7 set, ends a pass: unless the XOR of $8209-$8255 is $56, the result EOR $E2 is stored in $808F, which the SID writer adds to each voice's transposition and instrument offset, putting the music out of key. The text as shipped gives $56.
Write the immediate volume/filter value; the relocated loading loop fades operand $8A29 from fifteen to zero. Write filter cutoff and routing.
Operand byte 1 of the LDA instruction at $8A28, in the intro's code. Instructions in this part that name it: stx at $907C (write).
Three live little-endian order pointers, filled from the selected six-byte song header.
Three little-endian voice order pointers for song selector 0. The populated introduction song.
Three little-endian voice order pointers for song selector 1. All three streams are zero followed by $FF, rather than an additional populated composition.

Sixty-four interleaved little-endian pattern pointers. Indices zero through nine have multi-byte streams; the other 54 point at one-byte $FF terminators.

Eight-byte instrument 0: pulse width, SID control byte, attack-decay, sustain-release, wave-sequence number or interval parameter, vibrato or frequency-sweep parameter, pulse-sweep count and step (also the fixed frequency high byte), and behaviour flags. Record zero is all zero.

Byte 1 of instrument 0, zero like the rest of record zero. The driver names this address as the base from which it reads byte 1, the SID control byte, of every eight-byte instrument record, indexed by eight times the instrument number: lda $8AF7,X at $8536, lda $8AF7,Y at $861E and lda $8AF7,Y at $874D.

Byte 2 of instrument 0, zero like the rest of record zero. The driver names this address as the base from which it reads byte 2, attack-decay, of every eight-byte instrument record, indexed by eight times the instrument number: lda $8AF8,X at $8521.

Byte 3 of instrument 0, zero like the rest of record zero. The driver names this address as the base from which it reads byte 3, sustain-release, of every eight-byte instrument record, indexed by eight times the instrument number: lda $8AF9,X at $8527.

Byte 4 of instrument 0, zero like the rest of record zero. The driver names this address as the base from which it reads byte 4, the wave-sequence number or interval parameter, of every eight-byte instrument record, indexed by eight times the instrument number: lda $8AFA,Y at $85BD, lda $8AFA,Y at $86A2, lda $8AFA,Y at $86B3, lda $8AFA,Y at $86E5 and lda $8AFA,Y at $86F2.

Byte 5 of instrument 0, zero like the rest of record zero. The driver names this address as the base from which it reads byte 5, the vibrato or frequency-sweep parameter, of every eight-byte instrument record, indexed by eight times the instrument number: lda $8AFB,X at $852F, lda $8AFB,Y at $8816, lda $8AFB,Y at $8863, lda $8AFB,Y at $894D, lda $8AFB,Y at $896F and lda $8AFB,Y at $8985.

Byte 6 of instrument 0, zero like the rest of record zero.
